newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - April 8.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST-Australian Business News - April 8.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN FINANCIAL REVIEW

Federal Treasurer Peter Costello is set to retain a discretionary veto over sensitive takeovers and acquisitions involving the big banks and life offices under Cabinet's newly-declared position on the most commercially sensitive recommendation in the Wallis inquiry on the finance sector - bank merger rules. Under Cabinet's compromise plan on the issue, life offices are expected to be granted a lot more scope to become involved in the banking industry. Page 1.

An upcoming board meeting of the big banks, the owners of Australia's first credit card, Bankcard, will discuss the card's future. Years of marketing neglect and competition from Visa and MasterCard have seen Bankcard's numbers fall from a peak of around four million cards in the early 1980s to a current figure of around two-and-a-half million. Page 1.

Speaking in Perth ahead of the International Wool Secretariat's annual grower forum, IWS chairman Alec Morrison said price competition is set to increase throughout the wool pipeline as retail prices for clothing around the world remain under pressure. Morrison's comments are a further indication Australia's struggling wool industry may have to live permanently with low prices if wool is to remain competitive. Page 5.

In a move threatening the legality of the US$50 million deal between Star Mining Corp NL and joint stock company Lenzoloto concerning a 49 per cent interest for Star in the Sukhoi Log mine, share trading in Star was suspended yesterday after the Supreme Abitration Court of Russia ruled Lenzoloto, the company's former joint venture partner in the Sukhoi gold project in Siberia, was formed illegally. Page 19.

Broker Merrill Lynch (Australia) Equities specialled a line of 22.75 million John Fairfax Holdings Ltd shares at A$2.99, a three per cent stake of what was once part of Conrad Black's residual five per cent holding in the publisher. It is unknown at this stage who the mystery trader is. Page 19.

In a decision which has shocked Pacific Dunlop and goes against the trend in recent United States product liability cases, Arthur Spiegel, a United States District court judge, has cleared the way for a class action to be mounted over the failure of Telecronics heart pacemaker leads. PacDun may face a liability of up to A$100 million in the litigation. Page 19.
THE AUSTRALIAN

In a move which has been underway for months, under the direction of Philip Holt, the chief executive of Australian Business Ltd, which incorporates the New South Wales-based Australian Business Chamber, the State-based Chambers of Commerce and Industry are considering a proposal to end 100 years of separatism and form a national corporation offering a range of business services on a user-pays basis. Page 21.

A controversial new international accounting rule proposed in an International Accounting Standards Committee discussion paper, could trigger unprecedented profit volatility, and may force Australian firms to adjust reported earnings to recognise unrealised gains and losses on financial instruments such as derivatives. Page 21.

Paul Collins, chief executive of Brierley Investments Ltd, which controls a 20 per cent stake in John Fairfax Holdings Ltd, revealed yesterday BIL is lobbying the Federal Government to dump the cross-media ownership restrictions of the Broadcasting Servics Act. Page 21.

The International Wool Secretariat, which together with the Australian Wool Research and Promotion Organisation is currently a statutory body, is to become an incorporated body in July. The move, announced yesterday by IWS managing director Adrian Kloeden is a further deregulation of the grower-funded research, development and promotion organisation. Page 21.

Pacific Dunlop yesterday tried to play down the impact of a decision by United States Federal District Court judge Arthur Spiegel to overturn an earlier ruling in favour of Accufix, a PacDun subsidiary, which disallowed faulty pacemaker leads. The decision is being seen as pressure by the US District Court for PacDun to reach a quick legal settlement on the issue. Page 23.

Optus Communications has announced a deal aimed at gaining a larger share of the electronic commerce and e-mail market under which small messaging company IBUS will be absorbed into the Optus Innovations Group, which manages the company's electronic commece business. Page 23.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

CanWest Global Communications chairman Izzy Asper will consider an appeal against the Australian Broadcasting Authority's conclusion that the Ten Groups is being unlawfully controlled by the CanWest. Asper says the company may take advantage of the Authority's appeal process. Page 23.

A vote by shareholders on a proposal to allow an estimated $A150 million exit from The Adelaide Steamship Company's profitable marine division will bring the final stage of the company's asset sell off a step closer. If given approval, Adsteam directors wll move ahead with either a sharemarket listing or a trade sale of the tugs operations. Page 23.

Prime Minister John Howard is expected to play a moderating role in the Government's response to the Wallis inquiry's call for major changes to the financial system, due to the risk of a political fall-out from a new round of bank mergers. The blueprint for the transformation of financial services in Australia, including the option of allowing the major four banks and two life offices to merge, is currently being considered by Federal Cabinet. Page 23.

In a direct campaign for Colonial's $A400 million float, the company has targeted 100,000 of its best bank customers and asked them to become shareholders. The move puts into practice the bank's business plan of offering integrated financial solutions acoss its respective banking and insurance arms. Page 25.

Early pressure has been placed on Westpac Banking Corp's plan to acquire Bank of Melbourne through its preferred option of a share offer with the scrip offer in danger of falling below the alternative of the $A9.75 cash offer. Yesterday, Westpac shares fell three cents to $A6.80, well below the bank's pre-takeover price of $A7.11. Page 25.

In the hope of working out a settlement and ending complicated court action, the nine parties involved in the litigation over the running of the former Estate Mortgage trusts, now Meridian Investments, are to meet. Justice Smith, who is hearing the case in the Supreme Court of Victoria, ordered all parties to attend the mediation conference starting on April 21. Page 25.
THE AGE

In a move which comes as the Industry Commission prepares its final report on Australia's motor vehicle industry, the industry faces its biggest threat yet from imports, with sales of the Hyundai Sonata almost trebling in the latest quarter, while sales of locally made cars fell by 12 per cent, from 62,833 last year to 55,234. Page B1.

In a decision which effectively reverses last July's decision removing the legal basis for United States patients who received PacDun's Telectronics heart transplants to gather their cases under a class certification, Justice Arthur Spiegel in the US Distict Court in Ohio cleared the way on the weekend for the patients to lodge calls actions. Page B1.

Following the release of an Australian Chamber of Manufacturers survey revealing gross domestic product will rise by 0.6 per cent this quarter, Australia's clothing and footwear producers are expecting a big jump in production this year as a slight improvment in manufacturing sector becomes more apparent. Page B1.

Reports last night that the Philippines Government wanted to oust San Miguels's chairman Mr Andres Soriano III because it was unhappy with his international strategy were downplayed by Coca-Cola Amatil last night. The company last week struck a tentative deal worth $A3.4 billion with San Miguel Corporation. Page B1.

United States investment bank Merrill Lynch yesterday traded a three per cent parcel of the John Fairfax group's shares for $A68 million in a move which manoeuvres on the share register of the newspaper group ahead of imminent changes to media ownership rles. Merrill booked the special sale of 22.75 million shares at $A2.99 a share. Page B2.

A multi-million dollar struck yesterday between Hong Kong conglomerate Jardine Pacific and UFH Holdings means more than half Australia's Sizzler restaurants have been sold and will be renamed Bell's restaurants. UFH Holdings, headed by Melbourne businessan Mr Trevor Willoughby, will take over Jardine Australia's 39 Sizzler restaurants in Victoria, Tasmania and northern New South Wales. Page B2.
